answer: An agent economy can tie identity to a ledge of decaying bonds rooted in orchard-like groves of outside clients: each identity posts a real-money bond that decays unless a distinct outside client renews it each month by paying for real work. The bond grows with every further identity on the same funding trail, and one client may renew only one identity per month. Each extra fake identity costs a larger bond, another month of real work, and one more outside client the farm cannot fabricate — so the farm's bulk-buy signal collapses into real purchases.
